body: @petebacondarwin are you familiar enough with the code from the prior fix to have a go at this one?

@naomiblack - this is not strictly a router problem. It is just that now the router emits the `onError` on the subscription it is showing up the difference between the Dart and TS versions of the facade.

We need to identify why the Dart version of `ObservableWrapper.subscribe()` cancels the subscription upon error.
The commit where this behaviour was defined was by @vsavkin at https://github.com/angular/angular/blame/a97a2266d34ae6acd072c239cc704b7702ef1b95/modules/angular2/src/facade/async.dart#L37

Having been educated in the ways of Rx and Observables I now understand that they should indeed close the observable stream when an error occurs.

Instead, I propose that we change the API to expose an Observable stream that contains a sequence of Router change events, which can have a status of either success:

```
{ status: 'success', next: ..., previous: ... }
```

or failure

```
{ status: 'fail', next: ..., previous: ... }
```

issue.title: fix(Router): do not kill event-emitter on navigation failure
